## S8. Technical summary of the training video of the follow-up meeting: linear registration of ADNI data {.unnumbered}

In this video, the linear stx QC is examined through various examples of brain images. The reviewer evaluates each case based on scale, intensity, contour fitting, and symmetry. While there is some disagreement among the reviewers regarding the pass or fail status of certain cases, they discuss the limitations of linear registration in handling protrusions or asymmetries in the brain. They emphasize the importance of evaluating the accuracy of linear registration rather than purely relying on the image's appearance. The reviewers also discuss the impact of Z scale on assessing asymmetry, as well as the presence of shear or asymmetry in the Z axis. They analyze different data sets and debate whether certain cases should pass or fail, considering factors such as contour fitting and signal drop-off. The reviewer highlights the need for proper alignment using linear registration and provides detailed analysis and recommendations for improvement based on the intra-rater experiment results. The reviewer also mentions the feedback received from participants regarding the scale and shape of the brain, acknowledging the challenges in accurately judging images with slight deviations from the standard model.

(00:00:00 - 00:05:00). The reviewer goes through several examples of brain images and determines whether they pass or fail the linear stereotactic registration QC. The first example fails due to poor scale and intensity, while the second fails because the brain is too small compared to the contour. Another example fails due to scale issues in the occipital lobe. However, the reviewer finds one example to pass, despite some residual misregistration and a slight extension in the cerebellum. The group discusses the variability in the cerebellum, but ultimately agrees that linear registration is primarily focused on the cerebrum. The reviewer also notes the design scaling as a reason for some failures. Overall, there is some disagreement among the reviewers regarding which cases should pass or fail.

(00:05:00 - 00:10:00). The reviewer discusses the limitations of linear registration in the QC video and highlights that it primarily involves scaling and rotation, which cannot handle protrusions or asymmetries in the brain. They explain that if the scaling and rotation appear correct, there may still be small pieces of the brain sticking out because linear registration is not designed to address this. The reviewer suggests considering this when evaluating images with anatomical abnormalities. Furthermore, they emphasize that failing QC should not be solely based on the image's appearance but rather on the accuracy of linear registration. The subsequent section presents an example of a brain with significant asymmetry, particularly in the occipital area, where the right hemisphere is noticeably smaller. They note that while the left hemisphere fits well, the right side poses challenges in fitting the contour due to its size difference.

(00:10:00 - 00:15:00). The reviewer discusses the Z scale and its impact on the assessment of asymmetry in the brain. They mention that the orientation of the brain seems aligned, but there is a shear or asymmetry in the Z axis. The reviewer questions whether this shear is normal and suggests that it may be due to anatomical variability or local atrophy in the patient's brain. Despite this asymmetry, the reviewer concludes that the overall orientation and scaling of the brain are acceptable, and the images can be passed. They also note that the transforms used in the pipeline do not account for this type of anatomical variability.

(00:15:00 - 00:20:00). The reviewers are examining different data sets and evaluating their quality. They discuss the asymmetry in one data set, with an extension on the frontal and posterior ends, but ultimately agree that it should pass. Another data set presents a borderline case, with a possible issue in the frontal area. The reviewers debate whether to pass or not, but ultimately decide to pass it. However, they note that it is a difficult decision. They encounter a data set where the MRI appears small but fits well, except for some signal drop-off in the occipital area. It is another borderline case, but they lean towards accepting it as it is. They encounter a failure in a data set where the cerebellum appears small and there is an error in the rotation. Finally, they discuss a data set with a possible small rotation error, specifically in the Contour cutting through the occipital fat.

(00:20:00 - 00:25:00). The reviewer examines various data sets and evaluates their performance. In one case, the cerebellum does not fit well, suggesting an issue with the Contour at the Falk. The reviewer also notices a discrepancy with the Z-scale indicating potential problems with scale alignment. Another data set shows local misregistration between the Contour and the gray matter cortex of the MRI, but overall, it fits well. However, some rotation and scale errors are identified in other data sets, causing the Contour to cut into the occipital fat and extend outside the MRI, suggesting a failure. The reviewer highlights the importance of properly aligning the Contour and MRI using linear registration.

(00:25:00 - 00:30:00). The reviewer is discussing the results of the intra-rater experiment for QC on linear stx. They mention that the rotation looks good, and there is a small cerebellum observed in one subject. They comment on various aspects such as Z scale, X scale, Y scale, and Left-Right symmetry. Based on their observations, they determine whether each case should pass or fail QC. They note instances where the Z scale seems short or the contour is outside the brain, leading to a failure. They also mention cases where people failed due to X rotation and Z scale. Overall, they provide a detailed analysis of each case and make recommendations for improvement.

(00:30:00 - 00:35:00). Finally, the reviewer discusses the feedback received from the participants regarding the set scale of the images. Some participants mentioned that the scale appeared small, while others mentioned that the white matter was big. The reviewer then proceeds to analyze the Y scale contour, pointing out that the occipital pole had a slight extension, but overall, the contour seemed to fit the shape of the brain well. The Y scale in the front, back, and temporal lobe also appeared to be reasonably good. However, it is noted that some people might be offended by the Z scale since the cerebellum was not included within the contour. Additionally, the reviewer acknowledges that the shape of the brain being slightly different from the standard model could make it challenging to judge the images accurately.

## S9. Matrix of detailed inter-rater agreement of the raw MRI QC task {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: fig-agreement-raw
#| fig-cap: "Confusion matrix representing the percentage of agreement between the expert's gold standard ratings represented as E01 and the trainees represented as R01 - R09 for the QC labels given in the raw MRI QC task."
#| out-width: "80%"
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6

acq_count_plot <- copy(acq_99_count)
acq_count_plot[, Perc := as.numeric(gsub("%", "", Perc))]
ggplot(acq_count_plot, aes(x = Rater2, y = Rater, fill = Perc)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Perc), "%")), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#c7e9c0", high = "#006d2c",
                      limits = c(0, 100),
                      name = "Agreement\n(Percentage)") +
  labs(x = "Rater", y = "Rater") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## S10. Time measurements of raters for QC of the balanced dataset of raw MRI {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time-acq99
#| tbl-cap: "Measurements of the time to complete their raw MRI QC sessions (HH:MM:SS), number of rests, number of images assigned as \"Pass\" or \"Fail\", and the time spent per image divided by their assigned QC label (median and standard deviation; MM:SS) for the balanced subset of preselected cases for the trainees and for the two sessions performed by the expert (Ses1 & Ses2). Rests were defined as any time higher than 900 s (15 min) assumed to be time spent away from the computer and thus discarded for the timing analyses. Adjusted p-values show the significance of the different in timing between Pass and Fail ratings. The last row represents the median of the total time, number of rests, and number of \"Pass\" and \"Fail\" images, as well as the median time data by QC label among all raters."

acq_99_time <- read_rds(here("data/derivatives/acq_99_time_dt.rds"))
acq_99_time[Diff > as.difftime(15*60, units = "secs"), Rest := TRUE]
acq_99_time[!is.na(Rest), Diff := NA]

acq_99_summ1 <- acq_99_time[, .(N = .N,
                  Rests = sum(Rest, na.rm = TRUE),
                  Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(sum(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE))),
                  PvF = suppressWarnings(
                          wilcox.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating,
                                      na.action = na.omit))$p.value), Rater]

acq_99_all1 <- acq_99_summ1[, .(Rater = "All", N = 99,
                                Rests = round(median(Rests)),
                                Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(round(median(hms::as_hms(Session))))))]
acq_99_all1[, PvF := acq_99_time[, wilcox.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating,
                                               na.action = na.omit)$p.value]]
acq_99_summ1 <- rbindlist(list(acq_99_summ1, acq_99_all1), use.names = TRUE)

acq_99_summ2 <- acq_99_time[, .(N = .N,
                                Median = hms::as_hms(median(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE)),
                                Sd = hms::hms(sd(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE))),
                            .(Rater, Rating)] |>
                dcast(Rater ~ Rating, value.var = c("N", "Median", "Sd"))

time_format <- "%d:%02.0f (%d:%02.0f)"
acq_99_summ <- acq_99_summ1[acq_99_summ2, on = "Rater",
                            .(Rater, Session, Rests,
                              Pass_N = round(N_Pass),
                              Pass_Time = sprintf(time_format,
                                                  lubridate::minute(Median_Pass),
                                                  lubridate::second(Median_Pass),
                                                  lubridate::minute(Sd_Pass),
                                                  lubridate::second(Sd_Pass)),
                              Fail_N = round(N_Fail),
                              Fail_Time = sprintf(time_format,
                                                  lubridate::minute(Median_Fail),
                                                  lubridate::second(Median_Fail),
                                                  lubridate::minute(Sd_Fail),
                                                  lubridate::second(Sd_Fail)),
                              p = round(PvF, digits = 3))]

# Holm correction
acq_99_p <- acq_99_summ[, .(Rater, p)]
acq_99_p[, p_adj := p.adjust(p, method = "holm")]
acq_99_summ[, p_adj := round(acq_99_p$p_adj, 3)]

acq_99_summ |>
  gt() |>
  cols_hide(columns = p) |>
  cols_label(
    Rater = "Rater", Session = "Total Time", Rests = "Rests",
    Pass_N = "N", Pass_Time = "Time",
    Fail_N = "N", Fail_Time = "Time",
    p_adj = "p adj."
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Pass", columns = c(Pass_N, Pass_Time)) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Fail", columns = c(Fail_N, Fail_Time)) |>
  style_manuscript_table(table_type = "supplementary")
```

## S11. Time measurements of raters for raw MRI QC of the ADNI dataset {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time-acq-adni
#| tbl-cap: "Measurements of the time to complete the raw MRI QC of the ADNI data (HH:MM:SS), number of rests, number of images assigned as \"Pass\" or \"Fail\", and the time spent per image divided by their assigned QC label (median and standard deviation; MM:SS) for the expert and the trainees. Rests were defined as any time higher than 900 s (15 min) assumed to be time spent away from the computer and thus discarded for the timing analyses. Adjusted p-values show the significance of the different in timing between Pass, Warning and Fail ratings; values in bold are statistically significant. The last row represents the median total time and number of rests as well as the QC label and time data among all raters."

acquis_time <- read_rds(here("data/derivatives/acquis_time_dt.rds"))
acquis_time[, Rater := stringr::str_replace(Rater, "0", "-")]
acquis_time[Diff > as.difftime(15*60, units = "secs"), Rest := TRUE]
acquis_time[!is.na(Rest), Diff := NA]

acquis_summ1 <- acquis_time[, .(N = .N,
                  Rests = sum(Rest, na.rm = TRUE),
                  Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(sum(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE))),
                  PvWvF = suppressWarnings(
                            kruskal.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating,
                                         na.action = na.omit))$p.value), Rater]

acquis_all1 <- acquis_summ1[, .(Rater = "All", N = sum(N),
                                Rests = round(median(Rests)),
                                Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(round(median(hms::as_hms(Session))))))]
acquis_all1[, PvWvF := acquis_time[, kruskal.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating,
                                                  na.action = na.omit)$p.value]]
acquis_summ1 <- rbindlist(list(acquis_summ1[order(Rater)], acquis_all1), use.names = TRUE)

acquis_summ2 <- acquis_time[, .(N = .N,
                                Median = hms::as_hms(median(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE)),
                                Sd = hms::hms(sd(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE))),
                            .(Rater, Rating)] |>
                dcast(Rater ~ Rating, value.var = c("N", "Median", "Sd"))

# Build summary with Pass, Warning, and Fail columns
acquis_summ <- acquis_summ1[acquis_summ2, on = "Rater"]
# Replace NA with 0 for Warning counts
acquis_summ[is.na(N_Warning), N_Warning := 0L]
acquis_summ[, `:=`(
  Pass_N = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", N_Pass, round(N_Pass / N * 100)),
  Pass_Time = sprintf(time_format,
                      lubridate::minute(Median_Pass),
                      lubridate::second(Median_Pass),
                      lubridate::minute(Sd_Pass),
                      lubridate::second(Sd_Pass)),
  Warn_N = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", N_Warning, round(N_Warning / N * 100)),
  Warn_Time = fifelse(is.na(Median_Warning), "-",
                sprintf(time_format,
                        lubridate::minute(Median_Warning),
                        lubridate::second(Median_Warning),
                        lubridate::minute(Sd_Warning),
                        lubridate::second(Sd_Warning))),
  Fail_N = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", N_Fail, round(N_Fail / N * 100)),
  Fail_Time = sprintf(time_format,
                      lubridate::minute(Median_Fail),
                      lubridate::second(Median_Fail),
                      lubridate::minute(Sd_Fail),
                      lubridate::second(Sd_Fail)),
  p = PvWvF
)]

# Holm correction
acquis_p <- acquis_summ[, .(Rater, p)]
acquis_p[, p_adj := p.adjust(p, method = "holm")]
acquis_summ[, p_adj := acquis_p$p_adj]
# Format p-values
acquis_summ[, p := fifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))]
acquis_summ[, p_adj := fifelse(as.numeric(p_adj) < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(p_adj)))]

acquis_summ[, .(Rater, Session, Rests, Pass_N, Pass_Time,
                Warn_N, Warn_Time, Fail_N, Fail_Time, p, p_adj)] |>
  gt() |>
  cols_hide(columns = p) |>
  cols_label(
    Rater = "Rater", Session = "Total Time", Rests = "Rests",
    Pass_N = "N", Pass_Time = "Time",
    Warn_N = "N", Warn_Time = "Time",
    Fail_N = "N", Fail_Time = "Time",
    p_adj = "p adj."
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Pass", columns = c(Pass_N, Pass_Time), id = "spanner_pass") |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Warning", columns = c(Warn_N, Warn_Time), id = "spanner_warn") |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Fail", columns = c(Fail_N, Fail_Time), id = "spanner_fail") |>
  style_manuscript_table(table_type = "supplementary") |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = "8pt", column_labels.font.size = "8pt")
```

## S12. Post-hoc analysis of time differences by QC label in the ADNI data {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-posthoc-adni
#| tbl-cap: "Post-hoc analysis of the time differences by QC label of the ADNI data performed by the Dunn's test of multiple comparisons using rank sums using the Holm method for multiple comparisons. P values in bold are statistically significant."

# Per-rater Dunn's test with Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared
raters_posthoc <- unique(acquis_time$Rater)
raters_posthoc <- raters_posthoc[order(raters_posthoc)]

posthoc_list <- lapply(c(raters_posthoc, "All"), function(r) {
  if (r == "All") {
    dt_sub <- acquis_time[!is.na(Diff)]
  } else {
    dt_sub <- acquis_time[Rater == r & !is.na(Diff)]
  }

  # Only run if there are at least 3 rating levels (Pass, Warning, Fail)
  rating_levels <- unique(dt_sub$Rating)
  if (length(rating_levels) < 3) return(NULL)

  # Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared
  kw <- suppressWarnings(kruskal.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating, data = dt_sub))

  # Dunn's test
  dtest <- suppressMessages(
    dunn.test::dunn.test(as.numeric(dt_sub$Diff), dt_sub$Rating,
                         method = "holm", table = FALSE,
                         list = FALSE, kw = FALSE)
  )

  data.table(
    Rater = c(r, rep("", length(dtest$Z) - 1)),
    Chi_squared = c(round(kw$statistic, 3), rep(NA_real_, length(dtest$Z) - 1)),
    Z = round(dtest$Z, 3),
    p = dtest$P,
    p_adj = dtest$P.adjusted,
    Comparisons = dtest$comparisons
  )
})

posthoc_dt <- rbindlist(posthoc_list)
posthoc_dt[, p_fmt := fifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))]
posthoc_dt[, p_adj_fmt := fifelse(p_adj < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_adj))]

posthoc_dt[, .(Rater, Chi_squared, Z, p = p_fmt, p_adj = p_adj_fmt, Comparisons)] |>
  gt() |>
  cols_hide(columns = p) |>
  cols_label(
    Rater = "Rater", Chi_squared = "Chi-squared",
    Z = "Z", p_adj = "p adj.", Comparisons = "Comparisons"
  ) |>
  style_manuscript_table(table_type = "supplementary")
```

```{r}
                      name = "Agreement\n(Percentage)") +
  labs(x = "Rater", y = "Rater") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## S14. Time measurements of raters for QC of the balanced dataset of linear registration {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time-reg99
#| tbl-cap: "Measurements of the time to complete the linear registration QC (HH:MM:SS), number of rests, number of images assigned as \"Pass\" or \"Fail\", and the time spent per image divided by their assigned QC label (median and standard deviation; MM:SS) for the balanced subset of preselected cases for the trainees and for the two sessions performed by the expert (Ses1 & Ses2). Rests were defined as any time higher than 900 s (15 min) assumed to be time spent away from the computer and thus discarded for the timing analyses. Adjusted p-values show the significance of the different in timing between Pass and Fail ratings; values in bold are statistically significant. The last row represents the median total time and number of rests as well as the QC label and time data among all raters."

reg_99_time <- read_rds(here("data/derivatives/reg_99_time_dt.rds"))
reg_99_time[Diff > as.difftime(15*60, units = "secs"), Rest := TRUE]
reg_99_time[!is.na(Rest), Diff := NA]

reg_99_summ1 <- reg_99_time[, .(N = .N,
                  Rests = sum(Rest, na.rm = TRUE),
                  Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(sum(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE))),
                  PvF = suppressWarnings(
                          wilcox.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating,
                                      na.action = na.omit))$p.value), Rater]

reg_99_all1 <- reg_99_summ1[, .(Rater = "All", N = 99,
                                Rests = round(median(Rests)),
                                Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(round(median(hms::as_hms(Session))))))]
reg_99_all1[, PvF := reg_99_time[, wilcox.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating,
                                               na.action = na.omit)$p.value]]
reg_99_summ1 <- rbindlist(list(reg_99_summ1, reg_99_all1), use.names = TRUE)

reg_99_summ2 <- reg_99_time[, .(N = .N,
                                Median = hms::as_hms(median(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE)),
                                Sd = hms::hms(sd(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE))),
                            .(Rater, Rating)] |>
                dcast(Rater ~ Rating, value.var = c("N", "Median", "Sd"))

reg_99_summ <- reg_99_summ1[reg_99_summ2, on = "Rater",
                            .(Rater, Session, Rests,
                              Pass_N = round(N_Pass),
                              Pass_Time = sprintf(time_format,
                                                  lubridate::minute(Median_Pass),
                                                  lubridate::second(Median_Pass),
                                                  lubridate::minute(Sd_Pass),
                                                  lubridate::second(Sd_Pass)),
                              Fail_N = round(N_Fail),
                              Fail_Time = sprintf(time_format,
                                                  lubridate::minute(Median_Fail),
                                                  lubridate::second(Median_Fail),
                                                  lubridate::minute(Sd_Fail),
                                                  lubridate::second(Sd_Fail)),
                              p = round(PvF, digits = 3))]

reg_99_p <- reg_99_summ[, .(Rater, p)]
reg_99_p[, p_adj := p.adjust(p, method = "holm")]
reg_99_summ[, p_adj := round(reg_99_p$p_adj, 3)]

reg_99_summ |>
  gt() |>
  cols_hide(columns = p) |>
  cols_label(
    Rater = "Rater", Session = "Total Time", Rests = "Rests",
    Pass_N = "N", Pass_Time = "Time",
    Fail_N = "N", Fail_Time = "Time",
    p_adj = "p adj."
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Pass", columns = c(Pass_N, Pass_Time)) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Fail", columns = c(Fail_N, Fail_Time)) |>
  style_manuscript_table(table_type = "supplementary")
```

## S15. Change before and after protocol refinement of linear registration {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-prepost
#| tbl-cap: "Change in QC before and after the interruption of the linear registration QC of the ADNI data. QC labels of the images already evaluated before the task interruption and after the protocol refinement (n and percentage of the total). The images flagged as \"Warning\" were not considered when calculating the number of images changed."

# Compare pre-meeting and final ratings
reg_pre_final <- reg_pre[regis[, .(Image, Final = Rating, Rater)],
                         on = .(Image, Rater), nomatch = 0]
reg_pre_final[, Rater := stringr::str_replace(Rater, "0", "-")]

# Before counts (pre-meeting ratings)
before_summ <- reg_pre_final[, .(
  Before_Pass = sum(Rating == "Pass"),
  Before_Warning = sum(Rating == "Warning"),
  Before_Fail = sum(Rating == "Fail"),
  N_total = .N
), Rater]

# After counts (final ratings) - only Pass/Fail
after_summ <- reg_pre_final[, .(
  After_Pass = sum(Final == "Pass"),
  After_Fail = sum(Final == "Fail")
), Rater]

# Images changed (excluding Warning from pre-meeting)
changed_summ <- reg_pre_final[Rating != "Warning", .(
  Images_changed = sum(Rating != Final)
), Rater]

prepost <- before_summ[after_summ, on = "Rater"][changed_summ, on = "Rater"]

# Format with n (%)
prepost[, `:=`(
  Before_Pass_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", Before_Pass, round(Before_Pass / N_total * 100)),
  Before_Warning_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", Before_Warning, round(Before_Warning / N_total * 100)),
  Before_Fail_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", Before_Fail, round(Before_Fail / N_total * 100)),
  After_Pass_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", After_Pass, round(After_Pass / N_total * 100)),
  After_Fail_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", After_Fail, round(After_Fail / N_total * 100)),
  Images_changed_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", Images_changed, round(Images_changed / N_total * 100))
)]

# Average row
avg_row <- prepost[, .(
  Rater = "Average",
  Before_Pass_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", round(mean(Before_Pass)), round(mean(Before_Pass / N_total * 100))),
  Before_Warning_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", round(mean(Before_Warning)), round(mean(Before_Warning / N_total * 100))),
  Before_Fail_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", round(mean(Before_Fail)), round(mean(Before_Fail / N_total * 100))),
  After_Pass_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", round(mean(After_Pass)), round(mean(After_Pass / N_total * 100))),
  After_Fail_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", round(mean(After_Fail)), round(mean(After_Fail / N_total * 100))),
  Images_changed_fmt = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", round(mean(Images_changed)), round(mean(Images_changed / N_total * 100)))
)]

rbindlist(list(
  prepost[, .(Rater, Before_Pass_fmt, Before_Warning_fmt, Before_Fail_fmt,
              After_Pass_fmt, After_Fail_fmt, Images_changed_fmt)],
  avg_row
)) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    Rater = "Rater",
    Before_Pass_fmt = "Pass", Before_Warning_fmt = "Warning", Before_Fail_fmt = "Fail",
    After_Pass_fmt = "Pass", After_Fail_fmt = "Fail",
    Images_changed_fmt = "Images changed"
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Before", columns = c(Before_Pass_fmt, Before_Warning_fmt, Before_Fail_fmt)) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "After", columns = c(After_Pass_fmt, After_Fail_fmt)) |>
  style_manuscript_table(table_type = "supplementary")
```

## S16. Time measurements for the linear registration QC of the ADNI data {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time-reg-adni
#| tbl-cap: "Measurements of the time to complete the linear registration QC (HH:MM:SS), number of rests, number of images assigned as \"Pass\" or \"Fail\", and the time spent per image divided by their assigned QC label (median and standard deviation; MM:SS) for the ADNI data. Rests were defined as any time higher than 900 s (15 min) assumed to be time spent away from the computer and thus discarded for the timing analyses. Adjusted p-values show the significance of the different in timing between Pass and Fail ratings; values in bold are statistically significant. The last row represents the median total time and number rests as well as the QC label and time data among all raters."

regis_time <- read_rds(here("data/derivatives/regis_time_dt.rds"))
regis_time[, Rater := stringr::str_replace(Rater, "0", "-")]
regis_time[Diff > as.difftime(15*60, units = "secs"), Rest := TRUE]
regis_time[!is.na(Rest), Diff := NA]

regis_summ1 <- regis_time[, .(N = .N,
                  Rests = sum(Rest, na.rm = TRUE),
                  Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(sum(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE))),
                  PvF = suppressWarnings(
                          wilcox.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating,
                                      na.action = na.omit))$p.value), Rater]

regis_all1 <- regis_summ1[, .(Rater = "All", N = sum(N),
                              Rests = round(median(Rests)),
                              Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(round(median(hms::as_hms(Session))))))]
regis_all1[, PvF := regis_time[, wilcox.test(as.numeric(Diff) ~ Rating,
                                             na.action = na.omit)$p.value]]
regis_summ1 <- rbindlist(list(regis_summ1[order(Rater)], regis_all1), use.names = TRUE)

regis_summ2 <- regis_time[, .(N = .N,
                              Median = hms::as_hms(median(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE)),
                              Sd = hms::hms(sd(as.numeric(Diff), na.rm = TRUE))),
                          .(Rater, Rating)] |>
               dcast(Rater ~ Rating, value.var = c("N", "Median", "Sd"))

regis_summ <- regis_summ1[regis_summ2, on = "Rater",
                          .(Rater, Session, Rests,
                            Pass_N = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", round(N_Pass), round(N_Pass / N * 100)),
                            Pass_Time = sprintf(time_format,
                                                lubridate::minute(Median_Pass),
                                                lubridate::second(Median_Pass),
                                                lubridate::minute(Sd_Pass),
                                                lubridate::second(Sd_Pass)),
                            Fail_N = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", round(N_Fail), round(N_Fail / N * 100)),
                            Fail_Time = sprintf(time_format,
                                                lubridate::minute(Median_Fail),
                                                lubridate::second(Median_Fail),
                                                lubridate::minute(Sd_Fail),
                                                lubridate::second(Sd_Fail)),
                            p = PvF)]

regis_p <- regis_summ[, .(Rater, p)]
regis_p[, p_adj := p.adjust(p, method = "holm")]
regis_summ[, p_adj := regis_p$p_adj]
regis_summ[, p := fifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))]
regis_summ[, p_adj := fifelse(as.numeric(p_adj) < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(p_adj)))]

regis_summ |>
  gt() |>
  cols_hide(columns = p) |>
  cols_label(
    Rater = "Rater", Session = "Total Time", Rests = "Rests",
    Pass_N = "N", Pass_Time = "Time",
    Fail_N = "N", Fail_Time = "Time",
    p_adj = "p adj."
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Pass", columns = c(Pass_N, Pass_Time)) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Fail", columns = c(Fail_N, Fail_Time)) |>
  style_manuscript_table(table_type = "supplementary")
```

## S17. Time measurements of experts for the skull segmentation QC of the ADNI data {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time-seg
#| tbl-cap: "Measurements of the time to complete the skull segmentation QC (HH:MM:SS), number of rests, number of images assigned as \"Pass\" or \"Fail\", and the time spent per image divided by their assigned QC label (median and standard deviation; MM:SS) for the ADNI data. Rests were defined as any time higher than 900 s (15 min) assumed to be time spent away from the computer and thus discarded for the timing analyses. Adjusted p-values show the significance of the different in timing between Pass and Fail ratings; values in bold are statistically significant."

rskull_time <- copy(rskull)
rskull_time[, Rater := stringr::str_replace(Rater, "0", "-")]
rskull_time[, Diff := as.numeric(Diff)]
rskull_time[Diff > 15*60 | Diff < 0, Rest := TRUE]
rskull_time[!is.na(Rest), Diff := NA]

rskull_summ1 <- rskull_time[, .(N = .N,
                  Rests = sum(Rest, na.rm = TRUE),
                  Session = as.character(hms::as_hms(sum(Diff, na.rm = TRUE))),
                  PvF = suppressWarnings(
                          wilcox.test(Diff ~ Rating,
                                      na.action = na.omit))$p.value), Rater]

rskull_summ2 <- rskull_time[, .(N = .N,
                                Mean = round(mean(Diff, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
                                Sd = round(sd(Diff, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
                            .(Rater, Rating)] |>
                dcast(Rater ~ Rating, value.var = c("N", "Mean", "Sd"))

rskull_summ <- rskull_summ1[rskull_summ2, on = "Rater",
                            .(Rater, Session, Rests,
                              Pass_N = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", N_Pass, round(N_Pass / N * 100)),
                              Pass_Time = sprintf("%.0f:%02.0f (%.0f:%02.0f)",
                                                  Mean_Pass %/% 60, Mean_Pass %% 60,
                                                  Sd_Pass %/% 60, Sd_Pass %% 60),
                              Fail_N = sprintf("%d (%d%%)", N_Fail, round(N_Fail / N * 100)),
                              Fail_Time = sprintf("%.0f:%02.0f (%.0f:%02.0f)",
                                                  Mean_Fail %/% 60, Mean_Fail %% 60,
                                                  Sd_Fail %/% 60, Sd_Fail %% 60),
                              p = PvF)]

# Holm correction
rskull_p <- rskull_summ[, .(Rater, p)]
rskull_p[, p_adj := p.adjust(p, method = "holm")]
rskull_summ[, p_adj := rskull_p$p_adj]
rskull_summ[, p := fifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))]
rskull_summ[, p_adj := fifelse(as.numeric(p_adj) < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(p_adj)))]

rskull_summ |>
  gt() |>
  cols_hide(columns = p) |>
  cols_label(
    Rater = "Rater", Session = "Total Time", Rests = "Rests",
    Pass_N = "N", Pass_Time = "Time",
    Fail_N = "N", Fail_Time = "Time",
    p_adj = "p adj."
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Pass", columns = c(Pass_N, Pass_Time)) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Fail", columns = c(Fail_N, Fail_Time)) |>
  style_manuscript_table(table_type = "supplementary")
```
